sections.admission_summary: Chief complaint: Chest pain, diaphoresis, dyspnea. Admitted for inpatient care.
sections.discharge_instructions: Get adequate rest and avoid overexertion. Cardiology follow-up within 1-2 weeks. Cardiac rehabilitation enrollment recommended. Take your heart medications (Aspirin, Ticagrelor, Atorvastatin) every day as prescribed. Do NOT stop them without consulting your cardiologist. Restricted activity for 4-6 weeks. Avoid heavy lifting. Gradual return per cardiologist guidance. Call ambulance immediately for chest pain lasting >15 min, dyspnea, syncope, or cold sweats. Low-fat, low-sodium diet. Weight management.
sections.discharge_medications: Aspirin 81mg PO daily x365d; Ticagrelor 90mg PO BID x365d; Atorvastatin 80mg PO daily x365d
sections.follow_up: Cardiology follow-up within 1-2 weeks. Cardiac rehabilitation enrollment recommended.
sections.hospital_course: Length of stay: 8 days (primary reason: Chest pain, diaphoresis, dyspnea). Main treatment: vasoactive drugs (Dobutamine); antithrombotic therapy (Aspirin, Ticagrelor, Heparin); other parenteral drugs (Nitroglycerin). Key procedures: Urinary catheter insertion (2024-06-15), Arterial line insertion (2024-06-15), Transthoracic echocardiography (2024-06-15), Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) (2024-06-15). Intensive care unit (ICU) stay from 2024-06-15 (hospital day 1) to 2024-06-20 (hospital day 6), then transferred back to the general ward. Significant results: troponin I 103.386 ng/mL [H] (prior 85.727; troponin elevation) on hospital day 2. Medication changes from admission: started Aspirin, Ticagrelor, Atorvastatin. Vital signs at discharge: BP 119/72 mmHg, HR 91 bpm, RR 17 /min, SpO2 97% (RA), T 36.0°C. Condition at discharge: discharged home, Barthel Index 70/100.

sections.adl_assessment: Barthel Index 50/100 → moderate assistance (Feeding 5, Bathing 0, Mobility 10, Toilet use 5)
sections.care_plan: Care plan: Nursing problem: acute pain (chest pain). Goal: Chest pain resolves and the activity level can be widened with stable hemodynamics and ECG. Observation: Observe the site, severity and duration of chest pain; check ECG monitor, vital signs and urine output; Watch for diaphoresis, dyspnea or altered consciousness with chest symptoms. Care: Keep the ordered activity level and mobilize stepwise as the cardiac rehabilitation plan allows; Give ordered analgesia for pain and check its effect. Education: Explain that chest pain or palpitations should be reported at once by call bell.
sections.nursing_diagnosis: Nursing diagnoses: acute pain (chest pain), decreased cardiac output, risk for arrhythmia and recurrent ischemia, anxiety.
sections.nursing_history: Admission reason: Chest pain, diaphoresis, dyspnea. PMH: Chronic ischemic heart disease (IHD), Hypertension (HTN), Dyslipidemia.

sections.admission_status: Hospital stay: 8 days. Admission reason: Chest pain, diaphoresis, dyspnea. Discharge criteria met.
sections.nursing_interventions_provided: Medication administration: 118 doses (5 drugs); Vital-sign monitoring: 145 sets; Oxygen therapy: observed on 79 sets of vital signs; Procedures: Urinary catheter insertion, Arterial line insertion, Transthoracic echocardiography, Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI); Cumulative IN 11856 mL / OUT 11208 mL (net +648 mL); Education: Explain that chest pain or palpitations should be reported at once by call bell.
sections.patient_education: Patient education: continuing prescribed drugs (e.g. antiplatelets) and watching for bleeding; cardiac rehabilitation and pacing of activity; calling emergency services if chest pain recurs.

sections.op_course: Operative course: emergency procedure performed, operative time 48 min. Outcome: successful
sections.op_findings: Body site: Coronary artery structure / Target vessel: left anterior descending artery (LAD) / Access site: radial artery / Pre-operative diagnosis / indication: Acute myocardial infarction, unspecified (I21.9) / No intraoperative complications
sections.op_postop_plan: Postoperative plan: ICU-level monitoring. Access-site hemostasis and distal pulses will be checked, and the ECG and chest symptoms monitored for recurrent ischemia.
sections.op_procedure_name: Procedure: Percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PCI); single major coronary artery (code 92920); operative time 48 min

sections.assessment: ED diagnosis: Acute MI. Chief complaint: Chest pain, diaphoresis, dyspnea.
sections.ed_workup: Labs: WBC 9779.0 /uL, PT-INR 1.0, AST 24.0 U/L, lipid panel pending, troponin I 85.727 ng/mL [H], CK-MB 72.8 ng/mL [H], BNP 127.2 pg/mL [H], creatinine 1.1 mg/dL. Imaging: 12-lead ECG (ST-T changes suggesting acute myocardial ischemia), echocardiogram (No acute abnormal findings within the imaged range), coronary angiography (Culprit lesion identified; indication for percutaneous coronary intervention), chest X-ray AP (Cardiogenic pulmonary congestion, consider left ventricular dysfunction from acute MI). Medications: Aspirin, Ticagrelor, Heparin, Nitroglycerin. Procedures ordered: O2: Nasal cannula SpO2 >= 94%
sections.hpi: 62 y/o male patient. Chief complaint: Chest pain, diaphoresis, dyspnea. Symptoms began suddenly and worsened rapidly; presented to the emergency department. History: Chronic ischemic heart disease (IHD), Hypertension (HTN), Dyslipidemia. ROS: no syncope, no sustained palpitations.
sections.physical_exam: On arrival: BP 121/75 mmHg, HR 106 bpm, RR 22 /min, SpO2 98%, T 37.5°C. General: drowsy, responds to voice, pale, diaphoretic, in distress from chest discomfort. Cardiovascular: regular rhythm, no new murmur or rub, jugular venous pressure not elevated. Respiratory: bibasilar crackles, tachypnea.
